docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Sonata is a Discord bot that allows you to retrieve album information and import ratings from RateYourMusic.

docs.title: 📋 Features
docs.text:
• Retrieve information about music releases.
  • Check user profiles and statistics.
  • Explore ratings within your Discord server.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text: Start by importing your ratings from RateYourMusic by using the !import_ratings command. If you have Last.fm, link your account using the !set_lastfm command to automatically use the release you're currently listening to in other commands. After that, you can then use the various commands to explore yours and the server members' ratings as well as information about specific releases.

docs.title: !artist_ratings (!ar)
docs.text:
Shows user's ratings for a specific artist, ordered by score.

If no artist is provided, the command will use the last artist you listened to on Last.fm.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• User – Select another user by mention or Discord user.
  • Artist – The artist you want to search for.

Examples

!artist_ratings Radiohead !artist_ratings @user Radiohead

Order of arguments

If an user is specified, it must come before the artist name.

docs.title: !best_rated_artists (!bra)
docs.text:
Shows the best rated artists, ranked using a weighted formula.

If no user is specified, this command shows the best rated artists across the entire server. If a user is specified, only that user’s ratings are taken into account.

Examples

!best_rated_artists !best_rated_artists @user

docs.title: !most_rated_artists (!mrr)
docs.text:
Shows the artists with the most ratings.

If no user is specified, this command shows the most rated artists across the entire server. If a user is specified, only that user’s ratings are taken into account.

Examples

!most_rated_artists !most_rated_artists @user

docs.title: release (!r)
docs.text: Shows information about a specific release from RateYourMusic.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• Name – The name of the release you want to search for.

Examples

!release !release OK Computer

docs.title: who_rated_release (!wr, !wrr)
docs.text: Shows a list of server members who have rated a specific release.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• Name – The name of the release you want to search for.

Examples

!who_rated_release !who_rated_release OK Computer

docs.title: best_rated_releases (!brr)
docs.text:
Shows the top-rated releases among server members.

Examples

!best_rated_releases

docs.title: most_rated_releases (!mrr)
docs.text:
Shows the most-rated releases among server members.

Examples

!most_rated_releases

docs.title: random_rating (!rdr)
docs.text: Shows a random release rated by server members, with an optional filter for high or low ratings.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• Filter: – Filter to apply to the random selection. Possible values are:
    • glaze – Only include releases with high ratings (4 or 5 stars).
    • roast – Only include releases with low ratings (1 or 2 stars).

Examples

!random_rating !random_rating glaze !random_rating roast

docs.title: album_of_the_year (!aoty)
docs.text: Shows the best-rated releases of an year for a specific user.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• Year – The year you want to search for. If not provided, the current year will be used.
  • User – The user whose ratings you want to check. If not provided, the command will check the ratings of the user who invoked the command.

Examples

!album_of_the_year !album_of_the_year 2025 !album_of_the_year 2025 @username

docs.title: !lyrics (!lr)
docs.text:
Fetches the lyrics for the track currently being listened to by a user on Last.fm.

Examples

!lyrics

docs.title: !set_lastfm
docs.text: Sets your Last.fm username to link your Discord account with your Last.fm account. This allows the bot to fetch what you're currently listening to for other commands.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• Username – Your Last.fm username to link with your Discord account.

Examples

!set_lastfm @username

docs.title: !ratings_rank (!rr)
docs.text:
Show a ranked list of users based on the number of ratings they have submitted.

Examples

!ratings_rank

docs.title: !profile
docs.text: Shows your profile with statistics about your ratings.

docs.title: Options:
docs.text:
• User – Select another user by mention or Discord user.

Examples

!profile !profile @user

docs.title: !import_ratings (!i)
docs.text:
Import your ratings from a CSV file exported from RateYourMusic. A file can be obtained by going here and clicking Begin export.... Then, attach the downloaded CSV file to the command. You can do this by dragging and dropping the file into the message box or by clicking on the ➕ button left of the message box and then select Upload a file.

Examples

!import_ratings <file>

Info

The import process may take a while depending on the number of ratings you have. Please be patient and do not try to re-run the command while the import is still in progress.

Warning

Importing ratings will overwrite any existing ratings you have in the bot.
